subject: Customer gating + pricing exception request — ACME LATAM deployment
messages:
From: Kate Hsu <kate.hsu@acmecorp.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 6 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Redwood deployment for ACME LATAM subsidiary

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for last week’s demo. ACME is ready to pilot Redwood for our newly formed LATAM subsidiary (ACME Soluciones S.A.). The use case is inference for supply-chain routing and predictive maintenance — higher token volumes than our EU pilot but latency needs are similar.

Two items I want to flag up front that will affect contracting:
- ACME Soluciones is a Mexico-registered entity; we also have ownership links to a small JV that does business in Venezuela. Can you confirm Redwood’s stance on countries with recent export control sensitivities?
- Procurement is asking for a one-off onboarding discount (we’re requesting 35% off year 1 committed spend) plus a short IP carveout for derivative models used only internally.

I’ve attached our standard KYC packet and the draft SOW. Can you advise next steps and who we should expect to work with on compliance/contract? Our timeline is tight — pilot start target is first week of January.

Thanks,
Kate Hsu
Sr. Program Manager, ACME Corporation
procurement@acmecorp.com
Attachments: ACME_KYC_Packet.pdf, Draft_SOW_v2.docx
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 6 Nov 2027 09:36:00 -08:00

Laura / Rishi / Vivek — forwarding ACME request. Key asks: 35% onboarding discount, IP carveout, and a pilot for the Mexico entity (ACME Soluciones). They disclosed a JV that has operations in Venezuela which could be an export-control/red-flag.

Commercial context (from my side): this is an enterprise ARR motion; potential first-year ARR ~ $420k if we convert. ACME has indicated exec-level pressure to start pilots quickly.

Requesting:
- Rishi: run sanctions/screening and confirm whether Venezuelan JV relationship triggers restrictions or an eligibility block. If it’s a concern, what remediation steps (contractual controls, geofencing, add’l auditing) would be acceptable?
- Vivek: if compliance clears, can we get an executive pricing exception for up to 20% onboarding discount & 3-month pilot? If a carveout is required for IP, need legal to advise acceptable language.

I’ve attached the KYC packet and SOW. Please loop Legal/Compliance chairs if needed.

—Priyom
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 6 Nov 2027 10:50:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Redwood deployment for ACME LATAM subsidiary

Priyom — thanks for flagging. Quick initial questions / notes (we should treat this as a gated deal until we clear sanctions/export controls):

1) Which legal entity will sign the MSA? Is it ACME Corporation (US) or ACME Soluciones S.A. (Mexico)? We need the entity that will hold the contract to be screened.
2) Please provide the UBO list and any registration numbers (Mexico RFC / tax ID). I don’t see those in the KYC packet.
3) The mention of a JV operating in Venezuela is a material callout. Even if Venezuela isn’t fully sanctioned across all categories, we need to determine: a) whether any officers/owners are on sanctions lists, b) whether goods/tech exported to Venezuela would be restricted.
4) Proposed mitigations we can consider: restrict data residency to Mexico region, model-use limitations in contract, enhanced logging and audit clauses, and periodic compliance attestations from ACME.

I’ll run a preliminary sanctions screen against the names/email domains once we get the entity details. If any hits appear, we’ll escalate to the export-control team for classification.

—Rishi
Head of Risk & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Team — commercial context to consider: ACME is a strategic account; losing pilot timing likely delays a broader rollout across their Americas operations. My ask: if compliance can provide a path (contractual controls + geofencing), I’d like to pre-authorize a commercial concession to accelerate the pilot.

Proposed commercial package (conditional on compliance clearance):
- Pilot: 3 months free (up to $25k of usage) to reduce time-to-value.
- Onboarding discount: authorize up to 20% off year-1 committed spend (not 35%). Any larger discount needs explicit exec sign-off.
- Carveout request on IP: we will not accept a broad IP carveout. Legal to propose narrow language that allows ACME internal derivatives while preserving model IP and redwood rights.

If this looks OK from compliance, I propose we escalate to Vivek for an exec exception limited to the above commercial package and conditioned on: (1) sanctions clearance, (2) data residency constraints, (3) an audit-rights clause and SLA commitment.

Forwarded the KYC and SOW to the thread — I’ll draft the pricing worksheet and update the HubSpot deal.

—Laura
Director of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 6 Nov 2027 17:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Redwood deployment for ACME LATAM subsidiary — exec decision

Thanks all for the context and Rishi for triage. I’ve reviewed the commercial ask and the compliance concerns. Decision and conditions below:

Executive exception granted (limited and conditional):
- Approve a commercial concession up to 20% onboarding discount and a 3-month pilot as proposed by Laura. No authority to approve 35%.
- Approve a limited, narrow license for internal-only derivative use, but Legal must draft language that explicitly: (a) forbids model rehosting/redistribution, (b) preserves Redwood IP and weights, and (c) requires ACME to provide monthly attestations of internal-only use.

Conditions (must be satisfied before signing):
1) Rishi: complete sanctions and PEP screening for the signing entity and UBOs. No hits allowed on denied-party lists. If there are any matches, stop and escalate to export-control team.
2) Data residency: contract must restrict production inference traffic and logs to a Mexico region (or agreed cloud region) with audit hooks visible to Redwood.
3) Contract: include audit-rights, enhanced logging, and a termination-for-export-risk clause. No carveouts that grant perpetual rights to our models.
4) Deal desk: update HubSpot with the negotiated concession (Deal ID: RDW-2027-ACME-489) and attach the SOW link. Legal to prepare redline of MSA with the required clauses.

Priyom / Laura — you can proceed to execute the above steps. If compliance clears with no hits, Legal will prepare the exception language and we can move to DocuSign. If any sanctions hits appear, we will pause and route to the export-control committee.

—Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference
